Zambian Automotive Workers Stage Walkout, Halting Production at Major Plants

A large-scale walkout by automotive industry workers has brought production to a standstill at several major manufacturing sites across Zambia. The strike, which began early Monday morning, involves more than 3,000 workers at key assembly plants in Lusaka and the Copperbelt, including those operated by Zambimotor Manufacturing and Copperline Auto Assemblers.

Union representatives from the United Auto Workers of Zambia (UAWZ) cited unresolved disputes over wage increases and working conditions as the catalyst for the industrial action. “After months of negotiations, our members felt there was no alternative but to exercise their right to strike,” said UAWZ general secretary Felix Chanda. He added that the union is seeking a 17% wage increase and improved safety protocols.

The immediate impact has been significant, with production lines idled and completed vehicle inventories reportedly dwindling. Zambimotor Manufacturing spokesperson Martha Mwale confirmed that all three of the company’s plants have suspended operations. “Our Lusaka and Kitwe facilities are not producing any vehicles at the moment. We are closely monitoring the situation and hope for a swift resolution,” Mwale stated.

Industry analysts warn that a protracted strike could delay deliveries to domestic dealerships and disrupt export schedules. “Even a short stoppage can have a lasting effect on output and order backlogs,” said automotive sector analyst Thabo Lungu. As the walkout continues, workers remain gathered outside factory gates, vowing to maintain their stance until management returns to the bargaining table. Negotiations between company representatives and union leaders are expected to resume later this week.
